operating_notes.text: Supply Chain became the largest business division for the company in FY26.
Managing Director noted healthy traction across 3PL, warehousing and multimodal logistics, supported by growth in e-commerce, quick commerce and omni-channel retail.
TCI Seaways took delivery of 500-TEU cellular container carrier TCI SETU for ₹178.82 Cr funded via internal accruals.
Completed tender route buyback of 1,562,500 equity shares at ₹960/share for ₹150 Cr; total promoter stake increased from 68.66% to 70.08%.
TCI Supply Chain Solutions became the largest business segment in FY26, crossing ₹1,862 crore in revenue.
TCI Seaways acquired 500-TEU cellular container carrier TCI SETU for operation in Nov 2026.
H1FY27 capex of ₹343.2 crore was primarily funded via internal accruals (₹295.4 crore).

timeline.summary: CRISIL reaffirmed CRISIL AA/Stable long-term and CRISIL A1+ short-term ratings on the company's ₹600 crore bank facilities.

Transport Corporation of India Limited rescheduled its Analyst/Investor Conference Call to October 30, 2026, at 4:00 PM (IST) to discuss Q2 and H1 FY2026-27 results, led by Managing Director Vineet Agarwal and Group CFO Ashish Tiwari.
TCI board approved issuing up to ₹300 Cr secured redeemable NCDs on a private placement basis.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,388 Cr, net profit ₹116.9 Cr (+3.0% YoY) (includes ₹21.7 Cr from discontinued operations; continuing operations ₹95.2 Cr).
TCI Seaways took delivery of a 500-TEU cellular container carrier named TCI SETU for ₹178.82 Cr.
TCI issued its post-buyback announcement confirming completion of its ₹150 Cr tender offer buyback at ₹960/share, subscribed 1.87 times.
TCI presented its Q2FY27 investor update, maintaining 10-12% growth guidance and highlighting the Supply Chain division's emergence as its largest segment.
Audio recording of Analysts/Investors Conference Call held on Friday, October 30, 2026, is available on the company website.
